description: I am interested in space exploration, technology, storytelling, and creative problem-solving. I aim to develop an innovative project that makes space science interesting and accessible to everyone. I am open to collaborating with passionate participants who enjoy learning, researching, designing, and developing creative solutions.
summary: Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an interactive, bilingual (English & Malayalam) digital children's storybook and educator kit created for school-age space enthusiasts (ages 7–11). Across the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and deep space, dozens of NASA landers, rovers, helicopters, and telescopes rest silently after completing groundbreaking missions. While young learners often hear only about active launches, our storybook brings 13 real off-world explorers to life—connecting their engineering designs directly to the scientific discoveries they made possible. Built from 10 official NASA Science and NSSDCA datasets, every chapter pairs whimsical storytelling with verified mission facts, clickable links to real NASA Martian wind audio, 360° panoramas, and 3D spacecraft models. To maximize hands-on learning and classroom accessibility, the book also includes a printable cut-and-fold MarCO CubeSat model, coloring and word-search puzzles, a Junior Space Explorer certificate, and a two-page Parent & Educator Guide.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

"Abandoned But Not Forgotten" translates dense planetary archive records into an engaging, story-driven educational package for ages 7–11. Guided by a curious young stargazer named Mia, readers journey through four cosmic chapters covering 13 real NASA spacecraft:

1. The Moon: Surveyor 3 (1967 soil trench tests), Apollo 11 Eagle & Laser Ranging Retroreflector (still measuring the Moon's 3.8 cm/year drift), Apollo 12 Intrepid & ALSEP, and Apollo 15 Falcon & the first Lunar Roving Vehicle (27.9 km drive).

2. Early Mars Pioneers: Viking 1 (1976 first successful Mars landing) and Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner (1997 15-bounce airbag landing and first Mars rover in Ares Vallis).

3. Modern Mars Explorers: Twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity (proving ancient liquid water on Mars across 7.7 km and 45.16 km), InSight & MarCO CubeSats (recording 1,300+ marsquakes and Martian wind), and Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (completing 72 powered flights).

4. Asteroids & Deep Space: NEAR Shoemaker (first asteroid orbit and landing on 433 Eros), Dawn (orbiting Vesta and Ceres), Kepler/K2 (discovering 2,600+ exoplanets), and Pioneer 10 (carrying Earth's plaque toward interstellar space).

Educational Impact & Accessibility:

- Bilingual Storytelling (English & Malayalam): Makes NASA planetary science accessible to both English-speaking readers and Malayalam-speaking communities in Kerala, India, and worldwide.

- Interactive NASA Media Integration: Embeds clickable links to real NASA Martian wind audio (InSight), 360° landing-site panoramas (Pathfinder), and interactive 3D spacecraft models (Ingenuity).

- Hands-On STEM Activities: Includes a printable cut-and-fold MarCO CubeSat paper model, a Mars coloring page and 10-mission word search, a bilingual Junior Space Explorer Certificate, and a 2-page Parent & Educator Guide with NGSS-aligned discussion prompts and an exoplanet transit flashlight experiment.

Tools & Workflow:

We synthesized mission timelines, instrument specs, and scientific highlights from 10 official NASA Science and NSSDCA mission records, drafted and translated the bilingual narrative, and designed both the 13-page storybook package and 7-slide demo presentation using Canva.
